evidence: The no-acknowledged-data-loss / no-delete-of-a-committed-referenced-object principle is formalized as the INV_NO_LOSS invariant checked across multiple TLA+ models, e.g. docs/superpowers/models/CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore.tla (grep confirms INV_NO_LOSS also in CaB140DangleMerge.tla, CaGcCondemnMarkerGate.tla, CaIncarnationCore.tla, CaRetiredInRun.tla), and by GC's clamp-on-anomaly behavior in src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.h (RoundAnomaly / clamped_shards, comment 'fold clamps surfaced (never wedging) this round').

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Parts/PartFolderAccess.h:272-276, CachedPartFolderAccess doc comment: 'Each primitive performs the protocol operation and owns the cache side effect: erase the affected view on success; on exception cache state is untouched -- except dropRefBestEffort ...'.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Parts/PartFolderAccess.cpp:264-303 CachedPartFolderAccess::buildView calls store->readManifestShared(...) (both fresh-mode and cold-CachedForLoad paths) with no catch-and-suppress, so a missing/corrupt manifest propagates as an exception (readManifestShared defined in src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasManifestReader.cpp:56); StrictValidate bypasses retention entirely per PartFolderAccess.h:224 ('StrictValidate never populates the cache'), i.e. it always re-reads/re-validates.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Parts/PartFolderAccess.cpp:159-168, CachedPartFolderAccess::getView: comment 'Absence is never retained ...' followed by 'if (!resolved) return nullptr;' before any cache population -- a negative/absent ref result is never inserted into view_cache.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefCatalog.h:161-192, CasRefCatalog::deleteCompletedRemoving/deleteCompletedRemovingAtSnapshot exact-CAS-deletes a completed Removing catalog row, and cancelStalledCreating exact-CAS-deletes a stalled Creating row once its creator fence is proven terminal -- together these ensure no catalog row survives once the corresponding namespace name is no longer live, across repeated create/drop cycles.

Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.cpp, CasRefCkpt.cpp/.h, ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp, and PartFolderAccess.h/.cpp (PreparedPartWrite::abort) for 'relink abort', 'exact-GET', 'fail-long', and wedge/remount text. Found general wedge/remount machinery (CasRefLedger.cpp:2524 'wedged slot ... the mount is fenced closed and a remount is scheduled') and the every-attempt ambiguous-PUT resolution rule (gtest_cas_ref_wedge_every_attempt.cpp), and PreparedPartWrite::abort's append-based cleanup (PartFolderAccess.h:190-194), but no single artifact ties an unresolved RELINK abort specifically to 'wedged until exact-GET resolution or remount' plus the landed-vs-never-landing PUT distinction as stated; cannot confirm or refute the precise claim.

Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.h/.cpp and CasPool.h for 'indexed snapshot', 'chunked snapshot', 'lazy snapshot', 'row cache', 'per-round ref index', 'decoded-body reuse', 'chunked namespace removal' -- none of these optimization mechanisms exist at HEAD; the snapshot path only has the single full tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce (CasRefLedger.h:243) with no chunking/indexing/caching layer, so the candidate list is still an unimplemented proposal.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.h:243 tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce is the only snapshot-publish primitive at HEAD and rewrites the full snapshot run each call (no incremental/delta variant); searched CasRefLedger.cpp and CasRefProtocol.cpp for 'log-structured', 'O(delta)', 'compaction' near snapshot code and found none, so the proposed O(delta)-write log-structured-run remedy is not implemented.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefCatalog.h:181-328 defines cancelStalledCreating (idempotently completes/cancels an interrupted Creating row), beginRemoving (Live->Removing), deleteCompletedRemoving (idempotent Removing completion), and reconcileStaleCreator (steps 2+3 of creation resumed by a reconciler onto a stalled Creating entry); src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CatalogLifecycleReconciler.h is the dedicated reconciler component for the Removing drain.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Formats/CasLayout.cpp:96-140 Layout::parseRefObjectKey uses rest.rfind('/') twice (right-to-left) to peel the id then the _log/_snap kind segment and rejects any other kind_seg value; CasLayout.cpp:142-162 parseRefCkptKey similarly uses rest.rfind('/') to isolate the trailing _ckpt<suffix> leaf and rejects anything else, refusing non-canonical/legacy shapes by returning std::nullopt.

src/Interpreters/InterpreterSystemQuery.cpp:1063-1072, case Type::CAS_DROP_POOL_MEMBER calls `ca->checkNotReadOnly("SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER")` before invoking Cas::decommissionPoolMember -- the same checkNotReadOnly guard other mutating CAS entry points use (also called for 'GC round', 'GC rebuild', 'GC start', 'writes' in ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp) -- so at HEAD the read_only check is NOT bypassed for this entry point, contradicting the claim.

src/Disks/tests/gtest_cas_ref_wedge_every_attempt.cpp:1146-1162, comment on TEST(CASRefWedgeEveryAttempt, CreationCkptSurvivesAConclusiveFirstRefLogRejection): explains cleanupOrphanedBirthCkptBestEffort deleted _ckpt via a fresh head() read at cleanup time (exactly the bug described) and states 'The cleanup was removed entirely rather than patched (see CasRefLedger.cpp's comment at the removed call sites for why a captured token does not close the gap either)' -- the token-binding remedy the claim proposes was explicitly considered and rejected in favor of full removal.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1281-1297 shadowNamespace/FREEZE routing shows CAS's BACKUP shadow tree is mirrored in-pool as refs under a 'shadow/' root namespace (Pool::listNamespaces("shadow/")), not as local filesystem shadow directories/metadata files -- confirming the technical premise that classic freeze-and-copy (which walks a local filesystem shadow dir) cannot work unmodified against CAS.
